vedic_reference.note: Anila is a name of the Vayu Devta, the god of wind in Hindu mythology. In Hinduism, Vayu is the god of wind and air, and he is considered the second most important deity in the Hindu pantheon. Anila is also considered the goddess of the north-east direction and the goddess of the spring season.

data.cultural_impact: In Indian culture, the name Anila holds a profound significance as it is connected to the god Vayu, the patron of wind, which is considered an essential element of nature. This name is often given to children in Hindu families, particularly in those that value the spiritual richness of Sanskrit names and the reverence for the gods.
data.spiritual_significance: spiritually, Anila is a name associated with the divine embodiment of the wind element, which represents the ever-changing and transient nature of life. In Hindu philosophy, the name Anila implores one to connect with the divine power of winds and embrace change, impermanence, and the cyclical nature of existence. The name encourages flexibility and resilience in the face of life's uncertainties.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Anila was a queen of the Vedic god Indra. The name Anila carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Anila was a queen of Indra, the king of the gods in Hindu mythology. She is mentioned in the Rigveda, one of the oldest Hindu scriptures.
